# Cycle19 PDE370–377: strongest acquired primitive and exact remaining gate

7 October2026. Worker pde_spectrum9, verified GPT-6.1 Sol/max. No nested workers. Pinned OpenAI mathematics release commit `adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a`. Only owned cycle19 paths changed. No contact, publication, paid services, commits or upstream code execution.

## Main consequence

Family374's midpoint/cell-moment mechanism extends to **every full-dimensional compactly supported log-concave source**, including nonsmooth densities and densities vanishing at the boundary. For `K subset B_R`, targets in one compact `Y subset B_L`, centered Brenier potentials satisfy

\[
 \|u_\mu-u_\nu\|_{L^2(\rho)}
       \le(2+\sqrt5)R\,W_2(\mu,\nu).
\]

Thus the potential constant is independent of density contrast, number of atoms, their masses and their separation. A layer-cake transfer of the convex gradient interpolation yields

\[
 \|T_\mu-T_\nu\|_{L^2(\rho)}
 \le {\sqrt3\over2^{1/3}}
       [12d(2+\sqrt5)^2R^2]^{1/6}(28L^2M_\rho)^{1/3}
       W_2(\mu,\nu)^{1/3},
\]

where `M_rho=sum_j integral_(e_j^perp) sup_t f(xi+t e_j) dxi`. No lower-density or bounded-log-gradient hypothesis remains. The original smooth-source derivation is in `notes/pde_spectrum9/cycle19/LOG_CONCAVE_MIDPOINT_STABILITY.md`; the full strengthened proof, exact hypotheses and literal independent gate are in `notes/pde_spectrum9/cycle19/GENERAL_LOG_CONCAVE_STABILITY_AND_OBSTRUCTION.md`.

This is an internally reconstructed deduction, with two scoped independent analytic reconstructions of the smooth primitive and a separate reconstruction of the source limit/interpolation. External validation and exact contemporary priority are **UNKNOWN**. The density-independent midpoint mechanism is consistent with known interpolation facts; we do not claim that mechanism alone is novel.

## Decisive obstruction and nearest contemporary comparator

A fixed-square, smooth positive source `f_n proportional exp(-n^2 x_1^2)` and two-atom targets have W2=1/n while the map difference stays uniformly positive. Their `M_rho=n/(sqrt(pi)erf(n))+1/2`. Therefore every density-independent uniform map modulus fails, and a one-third map constant must grow at least as M_rho^1/3 along this family. The theorem's source-concentration exponent is sharp in this precise sense.
